name: Two Balconies
hint: The hatch has two locks. Each balcony holds one.
why4: Both balcony plates must be held while two go down the hatch and hold the 2-plate below for the balcony pair; with three, only one goes down and cannot hold the 2-plate.
solution: P4 stands at x=27 (edge of the gap at x=28-29) with P3 beside, grabs P3, faces right and throws: P3 lands on the right balcony plate (x=30-32, height 3). Gate F (bottom half of the hatch) opens.
P1 stands at x=6 (edge of the gap at x=4-5) with P2 beside, grabs P2, faces left and throws: P2 lands on the left balcony plate (x=1-3). Gate E opens: the hatch at x=16-17 is open.
P4 and P1 drop through the hatch into the lower room.
P4 walks left over the 1-bridge (x=10-14), then P1 crosses after P4 is off it. Both stand on the plate at x=8-9 (2/2): the hatch stays open.
P2 and P3 jump off their balconies into the yard and drop through the hatch.
P1 and P4 step off the plate (the hatch closes; everyone is below) and cross the 1-bridge back to the right one at a time.

P2 stands at x=19 next to the key shelf (x=20-22, 3 high, everyone can walk under it); P3 jumps on P2's head onto the shelf, touches the key at x=21, jumps down on the far side; P3 opens the door at x=24; all four walk under the shelf and press Down.
Recovery: anyone falling in the lower pit respawns in the yard; two below stand on the lower plate to open the hatch again.
